# Sistemėlė

> Sistemėlė ("a little system" in Lithuanian) is an open-source, MIT-licensed, practical starter kit and admin panel for AI-native projects. Motto: "Don't ask your agent to reinvent the wheel." Every business app needs the same parts: sign-in, roles, an audit log, a CRM, quotes, invoices with correct VAT and gap-free numbers, stock, a website with SEO, a dashboard and an MCP endpoint. Sistemėlė ships them built, tested and documented, so an agent builds only what is specific to the business. One Cloudflare Worker serves the API, a server-rendered public website, the MCP endpoint and a React dashboard; data lives in Cloudflare D1 (SQLite); email goes through Resend.

## Start

- Deploy to Cloudflare in one click: https://deploy.workers.cloudflare.com/?url=https://github.com/aimantas/sistemele (copies the code to your GitHub, creates the D1 database, asks for ADMIN_EMAILS and RESEND_API_KEY, deploys; every push redeploys).
- Demo: https://sistemele.aimantas.com (public site) and https://sistemele.aimantas.com/app (dashboard). One click signs you in as the demo owner. Sample data, reset every hour; no email is sent.
- Run locally (Node 22 or later): `npx degit aimantas/sistemele my-app && cd my-app && npm install && npm run setup && npm run dev`, then open http://localhost:5173/app and sign in as owner@example.com. Locally, the sign-in link shows on screen and in the terminal.
- [Source code](https://github.com/aimantas/sistemele): repository with `AGENTS.md`, a README per module and the guides below

## Modules

Switch modules on or off in `sistemele.config.ts`. Modules never import each other's server code; they talk through typed events: an accepted quote marks the deal won, an issued invoice deducts stock.

- CRM: a leads inbox (new, contacted, qualified, or disqualified with a reason; owner, follow-up date, source; convert a lead into a contact and a deal in one step), contacts, notes, tasks, and pipeline stages you add, rename and reorder, each with a win probability for a weighted pipeline value
- Catalog and stock: products and services, stock ledger with receipts, counts and adjustments, low-stock alerts, public product pages with Product structured data
- Quotes: numbered quotes with VAT per rate that customers accept or decline from a private link
- Invoices: gap-free numbering, immutable once issued (correct with a void and a new invoice), VAT per rate, partial payments, overdue tracking, bank-transfer details, public invoice link
- Website pages and blog: Markdown pages and posts with drafts, scheduling and RSS; members and agents draft, owners and admins publish
- Dashboard: drag-and-drop cards, KPI metrics from every module, templates (Owner, Sales, Operations, Minimal), layouts saved per person

## Give an agent the setup

Paste into a coding agent (Claude Code, Codex, Cursor or similar):

> Set up Sistemėlė for <business>. Clone it with npx degit aimantas/sistemele my-app and read AGENTS.md first. Run npm run setup and adapt sistemele.config.ts: modules, locale, currency and business defaults. Switch off the modules we don't need. Finish with npm run check. Ask me before any remote command.

- `AGENTS.md`: rules, a map of the code and recipes. Claude Code reads it through `CLAUDE.md`.
- Module READMEs (`src/modules/<id>/README.md`): API, MCP tools, events and rules for each module
- Agent skill: `npx skills add aimantas/sistemele`
- Claude Code slash commands: `/new-module`, `/add-widget`, `/add-dashboard-template`, `/add-mcp-tool`, `/seo-check`, `/ship-check`

## Extend it

- Start from `npm run module:new <id> "<Name>"` and follow the shape of the CRM module.
- One module: a migration, Zod schemas, services that validate, call `ctx.requireRole` and `ctx.audit`, thin routes, MCP tools, pages and widgets, a README and tests.
- Modules never import each other's server code; react to typed events in `src/modules/events.ts`.
- Money is integer cents; VAT and discounts are integer basis points (2100 = 21%). The server computes every total.
- Never edit an applied migration; add a new one.
- No invented business facts in copy, seeds or structured data.
- Done means `npm run check` (typecheck, lint, tests against a real local D1) and `npm run build` pass, and the change is checked in the browser.

## Deploy

One click: https://deploy.workers.cloudflare.com/?url=https://github.com/aimantas/sistemele

From a terminal:

1. `npx wrangler login`
2. `npm run setup:cloudflare` creates the D1 database and applies migrations.
3. `npx wrangler secret put ADMIN_EMAILS` (your email; it becomes the owner)
4. `npx wrangler secret put RESEND_API_KEY`
5. `npm run deploy` (builds, applies migrations, deploys)

`APP_URL` can stay empty: the Worker uses the address it is served from. Set it once you add a custom domain.

Agents must ask a person before any remote command (`--remote`, `wrangler deploy`, `wrangler secret put`); `AGENTS.md` sets this rule. `npm run dev` uses a local D1 only.

## For AI agents at runtime

- MCP endpoint at `/mcp` on every installation (Streamable HTTP, JSON-RPC). Authenticate with `Authorization: Bearer <API token>` from Settings → API & agents; the token's role (owner, admin or member) limits which tools it can call.
- Each installation publishes `/llms.txt`, and its public pages answer `Accept: text/markdown`.

## Built in

- Passwordless magic-link sign-in; owner, admin and member roles; API tokens; audit log
- CSRF protection, security headers, rate limits, server-authoritative totals
- Server-rendered public pages with unique titles, canonical URLs, Open Graph, JSON-LD, sitemap.xml and robots.txt; preview deployments are never indexed
- Stack: Hono, React 19, React Router, TanStack Query, Tailwind CSS v4, Zod, Vite with the Cloudflare plugin, Vitest with a real local D1
